page: Microsoft Azure F2amds_v7 is a compute-oriented virtual machine driven by an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor operating on the x86_64 architecture. The server features 2 physical cores and 2 dedicated vCPUs clocked at speeds up to 4.5 GHz, utilizing a single thread per core architecture. Hardware cache consists of 48 KB L1 data cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache. Advanced instruction set support includes AVX-512, AVX-512 VNNI, AVX-512 BF16, and VAES. The configuration is equipped with 16.0 GB of RAM, supplying 8.0 GB of memory per core, and includes 236 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD storage. No discrete graphics processors are present.

Performance benchmarks show leading single-threaded compute metrics balanced by low aggregate throughput on parallel routines. The instance achieves top-tier results in stress-ng single-core processing (3755.98) and Geekbench single-core testing (2855.0). Single-threaded data throughput is strong, marked by top-tier performance in gzip compression (40.8 GB/sec) and bzip3 decompression (17.84 GB/sec). However, multi-core capacity reflects the two-core boundary, posting average marks in stress-ng multi-core (7494.68) and Geekbench multi-core (5146.0), alongside weak ratings in Clang compilation (5468.0) and multi-threaded decompression (35.43 GB/sec). Memory operations register 47.98 GB/sec uncached read bandwidth and 6.09 million Redis SET operations per second.

By delivering high CPU frequency alongside a generous memory allocation of 8.0 GB per vCPU and fast local NVMe storage, the instance offers balanced resource density for workloads that do not require wide parallelism. The obvious tradeoff is limited thread concurrency, which reduces efficiency for heavy parallel builds and larger language model inference. The F2amds_v7 is suitable for latency-sensitive single-threaded backend services, in-memory caching layers such as Redis, lightweight databases, and localized data transformation tasks.
description: Microsoft Azure F2amds_v7 is a virtual machine featuring 2 dedicated vCPUs from an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor clocked at 4.5 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. Designed with a 1-thread-per-core layout, it is equipped with 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding 8.0 GB per core, and bundles 236 GB of local NVMe SSD storage with zero dedicated GPUs. CPU features include AVX-512 vector extensions and VAES cryptography. In benchmark testing, the instance delivers top-tier single-core performance, achieving 3755.98 in stress-ng and 2855.0 in Geekbench single-core, alongside fast gzip compression at 40.8 GB/sec. Due to its two-core configuration, parallel workloads such as software compilation and multi-threaded decompression show constrained throughput. The combination of high single-thread clock speed, generous memory density, and local NVMe storage provides a cost-effective operational profile for single-threaded microservices, lightweight databases, Redis caching, and localized ETL text processing tasks.
